title: Node's job heartbeat stops a drive on one busy beat (lease-renewal)
body:
## Summary
packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts's heartbeat sets `lost` on ANY failed beat, including a store busy past busy_timeout, so one transient lock stops a healthy drive at its next boundary.

## Description
job-run.ts:207-214: `const r = fx.tx("heartbeat", ...); if (!r.ok) lost = r.error;`. The lease-renewal technique (software-engineering/job-coordination) says renewing at ttl/3 exists so that 'missing one or two renewals (a transient store error) does not forfeit a live executor's lease'. The Python half now does this (e3e8db2e, job_record.beat_once): busy misses one beat, anything else is carried. Fixed looks like: an `unavailable` (busy) result is skipped, any other error or a LeaseLost is carried. Out of this context's paths (job-queue-and-leases).

## Flow
- a long step runs while another process holds the write lock past 10 s
- one heartbeat tx returns unavailable
- lost is set; the drive stops at its next boundary with the job interrupted/failed though its lease was still valid

## Expected impact
A drive survives a transient lock instead of being stopped while its lease was live. Could break: a store that is permanently busy now stops the drive only when the lease actually expires (fenced writes still refuse).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - parity with the Python heartbeat and the technique
Before: Node 0/1 transient-tolerant, Python 1/1 (e3e8db2e)
After: 1/1 both
Method: simulation - read side by side; job-run.ts is another context's path
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a case in packages/kernel/test/job.run or job.core tests: an fx whose tx("heartbeat") returns unavailable once with heartbeatMs tiny; expect the drive to finish done, not stop

title: The cross-language suites skip green when CI has no Python 3
body:
## Summary
Six packages/kernel/test files (and the tests/next-server Python suites) `describe.skipIf(python === undefined)` and only console.warn, and the gates job runs them on the runner image's unpinned python3 with no setup-python.

## Description
packages/kernel/test/helpers.ts findPython (one copy since 50c5c313) returns undefined when no interpreter answers; every suite then skips and `npm run test:unit` exits 0. .github/workflows/gates.yml pins Python only in its separate `python` job. A runner image change would turn the whole cross-language protocol check off with CI green. Fixed: findPython throws when process.env.CI is set and no Python 3 is found (policy-tighten), and gates installs a pinned python via setup-python. The workflow is outside this context's paths.

## Flow
- CI runner image drops python3
- findPython returns undefined
- job.python/lease.spec/lease.mixed/events.python/styles.python/py.cli all skip; test:unit green

## Expected impact
CI stops reporting green over an unrun protocol check. Could break: a CI lane that runs test:unit without Python would go red until it installs one (that is the point).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a skipped protocol check cannot read as a pass in CI
Before: CI=1 with no Python: 6 kernel suites skip, exit 0 (by reading skipIf)
After: CI=1 with no Python: exit 1 naming findPython
Method: simulation - building the gate needs a vitest run under a PATH with node and no python, and the workflow edit is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
packages/kernel/test/helpers.ts findPython
packages/kernel/test/*.python.test.ts describe.skipIf(python === undefined)
.github/workflows/gates.yml (python only in the `python` job)
instrument: CI=1 PATH=<node dir only> node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run packages/kernel/test/py.cli.test.ts: exit 0 today (skipped), non-zero after

title: The Python heartbeat thread dies silently when its own connect fails
body:
## Summary
job.py `start_heartbeat` opens the thread's connection outside any handler; a connect failure (WAL refused, file gone) kills the thread with a traceback and the run never hears of it.

## Description
packages/kernel/py/job.py beat(): `conn = connect(self.jobs.path)` precedes the try/finally; lease.connect raises LeaseError on a non-WAL store or sqlite3.Error. Same class as e3e8db2e (a renewal failure that never reaches the work loop). job.py is at 399/400 lines (CLAUDE.md cap), and the fix needs ~+4, so it needs room first (e.g. the thread body moved beside beat_once in job_record.py).

## Flow
- Jobs.claim succeeds
- run.start_heartbeat(); the thread's connect raises
- no beat ever runs; _lost stays None; the run writes until its TTL lapses

## Expected impact
A run whose heartbeat cannot start stops at its next call. Could break: nothing a working store reaches.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every renewal failure reaches the run
Before: 1 path (connect) where the failure is silent
After: 0
Method: simulation - the site is at the 400-line cap; the move that makes room is M
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/kernel/py/job.py start_heartbeat beat(): conn = connect(self.jobs.path) outside try
wc -l packages/kernel/py/job.py = 399
instrument: a case beside the heartbeat cases in packages/kernel/test/job.python.test.ts with job.connect patched to raise inside the thread; expect run.start to raise LeaseLost

title: Python recover() re-checks every ended job of its producers on every start
body:
## Summary
job_settle.recover walks every done/failed/interrupted job of the worker's producers - all history - and runs settle() on each: 3 transactions per job (load, owed, record) even when nothing is owed.

## Description
packages/kernel/py/job_settle.py recover(): `ended = [... state IN ('done','failed','interrupted') AND producer IN (...)]` then `settle(jobs, jid)` per id; settle opens a tx to load, owed() opens another for two max(seq) queries. Cost grows with the store's lifetime, on every worker start. A single query (endings whose max(seq) of job.done/failed/interrupted exceeds the max(seq) of job.settled/settle-failed) would return only the owed ids.

## Flow
- a forge worker starts on a store with N finished forge jobs
- recover runs 2N+ transactions before claiming
- N=1000: measured cost unknown

## Expected impact
Worker start time stops scaling with history. Could break: an ending the one query misses would never be settled - the cross-language spec scenarios 'settles' pin the once-per-ending rule.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - recover cost bounded by the owed endings, not history
Before: 3 transactions per historical ended job (read from the code)
After: 1 query + 3 per OWED job
Method: simulation - no timing harness over a large store this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: time Jobs.recover(['forge']) over a Node-built store with 1000 done forge jobs and settled events, before/after; spec/job.json settle scenarios stay green

title: kernel_meter books a $0 cost on the chain and a vendor-reported $0 at the estimate
body:
## Summary
Python Meter.call writes `cost` on spend.booked even when the amount is 0, and treats a reported usd of 0 as unreported (books the estimate, basis estimate); Node's spend/ledger.ts `book` omits cost when the total is 0 and takes the basis from the entry.

## Description
packages/kernel/py/kernel_meter.py call(): `reported = isinstance(usd, (int, float)) and usd > 0`; append(..., cost={'usd': amount, ...}) unconditionally. packages/kernel/src/spend/ledger.ts book(): `...(cls.unit === 'usd' && b.total > 0 ? { cost } : {})`. A free call (vendor says $0) is booked at its estimate under Python - the Ledger overstates a Dojo judge - and a $0 estimate puts a cost:0 row on the chain Node would not.

## Flow
- dojo_judge calls a model that reports usd 0
- Meter books estimate_usd with basis estimate
- Node booking the same entry books 0, basis vendor, no cost on the event

## Expected impact
Spend rows agree across languages. Could break: a caller relying on 'unreported means estimate' when a vendor returns 0 for 'unknown' - the card must decide which a 0 means per provider.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one booking rule in two languages
Before: 2 divergences (cost at 0; reported 0 -> estimate)
After: 0
Method: simulation - the meaning of a vendor's 0 is a product call per provider
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/kernel/py/kernel_meter.py call() reported/append
packages/kernel/src/spend/ledger.ts book() b.total > 0
instrument: tests/next-server/dojo-judge-meter.test.ts case: Meter.call(call=lambda: (v, 0)) vs Node book with amount 0 basis vendor; compare spend_rows and the event's cost
drain_note: policy-loosen: booking a vendor 0 lowers recorded spend; a product call
